## ESMO 2026 Presentations Deepen the Evidence Base for Natera’s Oncology Portfolio and Leadership in Ultrasensitive MRD Technology


10/18/2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 142 KB](https://s201.q4cdn.com/354493536/files/doc_news/ESMO-2026-Presentations-Deepen-the-Evidence-Base-for-Nateras-Oncology-Portfolio-and-Leadership-in-Ultrasensitive-MRD-Technology-2026.pdf)


*Natera and its collaborators will present 20 abstracts, including 4 rapid oral presentations*


*Signatera* *™* *Genome with Phased and Structural Variants, which has achieved detection below 1 part per 10 million and an LOD95 of 1 part per million, will be featured in Natera’s ESMO program*


AUSTIN, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Natera, Inc.](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.natera.com&esheet=54624263&newsitemid=20261018851261&lan=en-US&anchor=Natera%2C+Inc.&index=1&md5=004d3a1635f37ae6bcbc34aadd01bb52) (NASDAQ: NTRA), a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, today announced that 20 abstracts featuring its technology will be presented at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Annual Congress, taking place October 23–26 in Madrid, Spain.


New evidence highlights the power of Natera’s latest ultrasensitive molecular residual disease (MRD) technology, Signatera Genome with Phased and Structural Variants, which has demonstrated an industry-leading analytical limit of detection (LOD95) below 1 part per million (ppm), and detection observed significantly below 1 part per 10 million.1


Spanning tumor types and treatment modalities, multiple ESMO presentations will show that serial ctDNA testing provides meaningful clinical benefit:


- *ICONIC trial in gastroesophageal cancer (abstract 2901P):* Among patients treated with perioperative chemotherapy and immunotherapy, MRD clearance during neoadjuvant therapy was strongly associated with a lower risk of recurrence and a favorable pathologic response. Signatera Genome with Phased and Structural Variants detected all evaluable recurrences during surveillance, with a >7.3 month median lead time over standard imaging.
- *SAGITTARIUS trial in colon cancer (abstract 808P):* In this phase III trial, post-operative patients were randomized to a physician-choice adjuvant treatment plan prior to receiving MRD results to assess impact. The analysis showed that Signatera results influenced a change to providers’ pre-planned treatment for one in three patients, of which 87% were treatment de-escalated based on MRD negativity.
- *Colorectal/Breast cancer (abstract 4258P):* In a retrospective analysis of surveillance monitoring of stage I-III breast and colorectal cancer survivors, serial Signatera negativity was associated with an extremely low 2-year recurrence risk, which may help refine risk stratification and inform eligibility for solid organ transplant earlier than current methodologies.
- *Breast cancer (abstract 1770RO):* In HER2+ metastatic breast cancer, an analysis of exceptional responders on anti-HER2 therapy showed 81% with sustained MRD-negativity during serial monitoring, supporting the potential for Signatera-guided de-escalation.
- *MDT-Bridge trial in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (abstract LBA62)* : This phase II trial evaluated MRD clearance from baseline to pre-surgery/pre-CRT using the Clarity ™ assay with *phased variant* technology.
- *MRD-guided reflex to liquid CGP drives actionable treatment decisions (abstract 4260P)* : In a cohort of 50 patients across 10 tumor types, Signatera, complemented by reflex to blood-based comprehensive genomic profiling (liquid CGP), identified clinically relevant biomarkers in 18 patients, including *ESR1, BRAF, FGFR3, and BRCA2* .


“We are pleased to share data at ESMO that highlights our expanding diagnostics portfolio, which includes the newest version of our ultrasensitive Signatera Genome test,” said Minetta Liu, M.D., chief medical officer, oncology and early cancer detection, Natera. “The incorporation of phased and structural variants results in the ability to detect ctDNA significantly below 1 part per 10 million and takes MRD sensitivity into a range we haven’t seen before.”

**About Natera**


Natera is a global leader in cell-free DNA and precision medicine, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. We aim to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard-of-care to protect health and inform earlier, more targeted interventions that help lead to longer, healthier lives. Natera’s tests are supported by more than 400 peer-reviewed publications that demonstrate excellent performance. Natera operates ISO 13485-certified and CAP-accredited laboratories certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) in Austin, Texas, and San Carlos, California, and through Foresight Diagnostics, its subsidiary, operates an ISO 27001-certified and CAP-accredited laboratory certified under CLIA in Boulder, Colorado.
